text.p: The following are some of the leading stories in Finnish papers this morning.
- After active lives in sport and work eight 20-year old horses will retire into a home for the aged in Porvoo, where they can watch birds and be visited by their owners.
- Finland massively beat Sweden in a bingo match between the two countries on Sunday.
- Real estate agents say prices of flats in old apartment blocks will continue to rise within the next year.
- Hermes Kreditversicherung AG of Germany, specialised in credit insurance, will be the first ever to enter the Finnish credit insurance market in the begining of next year.
- A new law to shift the duty of environmental protection onto forest owners and loggers comes into effect next year.
- Small banks install more doors as a new measure against raids.
- A year of being a listed company has brought efficiency into Neste, says company executive Jukka Viinanen.
- Finnish employers launch special campaign to encourage companies to provide opportunities for young foreigners.
